researchQuestion:
Main question: Among post-9/11 U.S. veterans enrolled in VA mental health care, how do attitude toward the behavior, subjective norm, and perceived behavioral control relate to treatment engagement?

Subquestions:
1. Does intention to stay in treatment explain these relationships?
2. Does the relationship between intention to stay in treatment and treatment engagement differ by distance to care?
hypotheses:
H1 (direct): Higher attitude toward the behavior will be associated with higher intention to stay in treatment.

H2 (direct): Higher subjective norm will be associated with lower intention to stay in treatment.

H3 (direct): Higher perceived behavioral control will be associated with higher intention to stay in treatment.

H4 (direct): Higher intention to stay in treatment will be associated with higher treatment engagement.

H5 (direct): Higher perceived behavioral control will be associated with higher treatment engagement.

H6 (moderation): The link between intention to stay in treatment and treatment engagement will differ by distance to care (under 30 miles vs. 30 or more miles from the clinic).

H7 (mediation): Intention to stay in treatment will completely mediate the links from attitude toward the behavior and subjective norm, and partially mediate the link from perceived behavioral control, to treatment engagement.
